reconstructed_theorem:
For every \(d,q\in\mathbb N\), every \(\kappa\in\mathbb R\) with \(\kappa\ge 2\) and \(2q+1<d\), and every real Euclidean coordinate array
\[
x\in\mathbb R^{I\times A},\qquad I=\{0,\ldots,d-1\},\qquad A=\{0,\ldots,q\},
\]
make the following definitions. Regard \(x_{i,a}\) as its unchanged real coordinate at the ordered pair \((i,a)\), and put
\[
\theta_i=\frac{(i+\tfrac12)\pi}{d},\qquad
\lambda_i=\frac{\kappa+1}{2}+\frac{\kappa-1}{2}\cos\theta_i,\qquad
\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_i)_{i\in I},\qquad
g_a(i)=x_{i,a}.
\]
Define a real \(d\)-by-\((q+1)\) matrix \(t\), and a real \(d\)-by-\((q+1)^2\) matrix \(B\) whose column indices are ordered pairs in \(A\times A\), by
\[
t_{i,k}=
\begin{cases}
1,&k=0,\\
\sqrt{2}\cos(k\theta_i),&1\le k\le q,
\end{cases}
\qquad
B_{i,(a,k)}=\frac{1}{\sqrt d}\,g_a(i)t_{i,k}.
\]
Here square roots are the nonnegative real roots. Define the subspace
\[
K=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}
\left\{\Lambda^k g_a:\ a\in A,\ k\in A\right\}
\subseteq\mathbb R^I,
\]
where \(\Lambda^k\) is the ordinary matrix power and its product with \(g_a\) is ordinary matrix-vector multiplication; in particular \(\Lambda^0\) is the identity. Then the actual image of \(B\) equals this entire subspace:
\[
\left\{Bc:\ c\in\mathbb R^{A\times A}\right\}=K.
\]
Explicitly, \(c\) ranges over all real coefficient arrays indexed by \((a,k)\), and \((Bc)_i=\sum_{(a,k)\in A\times A}B_{i,(a,k)}c_{a,k}\). Thus the left side is the set of all linear combinations of the columns of \(B\); it is not merely the set of those columns. The right side is the real linear span of the displayed vectors, not merely their set of values.

The assumptions imply \(d\ge 2q+2\ge 2\), so the denominator \(\sqrt d\) is positive. The case \(q=0\) is included: \(A=\{0\}\), \(t_{i,0}=1\), the only column of \(B\) is \(g_0/\sqrt d\), and \(K=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{g_0\}\). If every coordinate of \(x\) is zero, both sets are \(\{0\}\); zero vectors or linear dependence among the \(g_a\) are also allowed. The case \(\kappa=2\) and the smallest admissible dimension \(d=2q+2\) are included. Neither \(d=0\) nor \(d=1\) is admissible. The first and last angular nodes are \(\theta_0=\pi/(2d)\) and \(\theta_{d-1}=\pi-\pi/(2d)\); the angles \(0\) and \(\pi\) are not sampled. No distribution, independence, nonzero-coordinate, rank, or invertibility assumption is placed on \(x\), the \(g_a\), or \(B\).

plain_string_statement: For all natural numbers d and q, all real kappa with kappa >= 2 and 2*q + 1 < d, and every arbitrary real Euclidean coordinate array x indexed by (i,a) with 0 <= i < d and 0 <= a <= q, set theta_i = (i + 1/2)*pi/d, lambda_i = (kappa + 1)/2 + ((kappa - 1)/2)*cos(theta_i), Lambda = diag(lambda_i), and g_a(i) = x_(i,a). For 0 <= k <= q define t_(i,k) = 1 if k = 0 and sqrt(2)*cos(k*theta_i) otherwise. Define B_(i,(a,k)) = (1/sqrt(d))*g_a(i)*t_(i,k), with ordered column index (a,k) in {0,...,q} x {0,...,q}. Then { B*c : c is any real coefficient array indexed by (a,k) } equals span_R{ Lambda^k * g_a : 0 <= a <= q and 0 <= k <= q }, as subsets of the real vectors indexed by i. All matrix-vector products use finite sums; Lambda^k denotes ordinary matrix powers, with Lambda^0 the identity, and the span contains every real linear combination. The case q = 0 is allowed, d >= 2*q + 2 >= 2 is forced, kappa = 2 and d = 2*q + 2 are included, and x may be zero or have any linear dependencies. There is no probabilistic assumption.

objects.index_sets: I = Fin d = {0,...,d-1}; A = Fin(q+1) = {0,...,q}; ordered pairs (a,k) in A x A index the columns of B and the generating family for K.
objects.input: An arbitrary x in EuclideanSpace R (I x A), identified only through WithLp.ofLp with its unchanged coordinates x_(i,a).
objects.diagonal_matrix: lambda_i = (kappa+1)/2 + ((kappa-1)/2)*cos(theta_i); Lambda is diagonal with entries lambda_i and zero off diagonal.
objects.cosine_array: t : I x A -> R, t_(i,0)=1 and t_(i,k)=sqrt(2)*cos(k*theta_i) for k>0.
objects.column_matrix: B : I x (A x A) -> R, B_(i,(a,k))=(sqrt(d))^(-1)*g_a(i)*t_(i,k).
objects.subspace: K = span_R of the actual range of (a,k) |-> Lambda^k g_a.

domains.d_q: Natural numbers, including zero in their underlying domain; the inequality subsequently excludes d <= 1.
domains.x: Real Euclidean space on exactly the finite coordinates I x A.
domains.coefficients: All functions A x A -> R.
domains.scalars: Real scalars for all spans and finite sums.

quantifiers: Universally quantify d,q in N; kappa in R; proof h_kappa of 2 <= kappa; proof h_q of 2*q+1 < d; and every x in EuclideanSpace R (Fin d x Fin(q+1)). All later symbols are local definitions, not existentially selected witnesses. The range quantifies over every real coefficient array c. The generating range quantifies over every ordered pair (a,k).
assumptions: No other hypothesis on x, including no probability distribution, independence, nondegeneracy, normalization, full rank, or nonzero-coordinate hypothesis.
The packet reports compiled=true; that report has not been independently checked and adds no mathematical premise.
conclusion: As literal sets of real vectors indexed by I, the actual image {B.mulVec(c) : c : A x A -> R} equals the underlying set of K. This is the image of an entire linear coefficient map and the entire real linear span, not equality of the two raw column/generator families and not a claim about probability or only generic inputs.

scopes.arithmetic: All displayed arithmetic in theta, eigenvalues, t and B is real arithmetic; finite index values and d are cast to R. Real inverse is the field inverse; the assumptions ensure d>0 in this instance.
scopes.powers: Lambda^k is the ordinary matrix product power, not an entrywise power of a general matrix. Its zero power is the identity, so the k=0 generators are g_a. For the diagonal Lambda, its action can also be written componentwise as lambda_i^k*g_a(i), including the zero exponent convention.
scopes.normalization: Angles are the d midpoint nodes (i+1/2)*pi/d. The k=0 cosine column equals exactly 1, while k>0 carries exactly sqrt(2). Every B column has exactly the common real factor 1/sqrt(d). There is no extra scaling in g_a, the eigenvalues, Lambda or K.
scopes.coordinate_order: x is indexed first by row i and second by vector label a. A B column index has first component a selecting g_a and second component k selecting the cosine degree. That same second component supplies the matrix exponent in K. No arbitrary flattening order is needed or asserted.
scopes.span_and_image: Set.range denotes the actual set of values. K is the real linear span of the generating range. The left range is already the set of all real linear combinations of B's columns because c is unrestricted.
zero_and_boundary_cases: q=0 is admissible precisely when d>1; then B has the single column g_0/sqrt(d), and K=span_R{g_0}.
d=0 and d=1 are excluded, and the smallest admissible dimension for a given q is d=2*q+2.
kappa=2 is included; no strict lower bound, upper bound, integrality, or finiteness condition beyond being a real number is imposed on kappa.
k=0 is always present and uses the identity power; if q>0, k=q is also present.

The first and last rows use theta_0=pi/(2*d) and theta_(d-1)=pi-pi/(2*d); 0 and pi are not angular nodes. In particular the eigenvalue formula is sampled at those interior cosine nodes, not at the endpoint angles.
The all-zero x gives B=0 and K={0}; arbitrary partially zero or linearly dependent g_a are allowed.

constant_dependencies.theta: Depends on d and i; pi is the fixed real circle constant.
constant_dependencies.eigenvalue_Lambda: Depend on kappa and d (and row index for eigenvalue).
constant_dependencies.g: Depends on x and its d-by-(q+1) coordinate shape.
constant_dependencies.t: Depends on d, q and its indices; independent of x and kappa.
constant_dependencies.B: Depends on d, q and x; its literal formula is independent of kappa.
constant_dependencies.K: Depends on d, q, kappa and x.
constant_dependencies.conclusion: Quantified jointly for every admissible tuple (d,q,kappa,x); h_kappa and h_q are proofs of assumptions, not extra numerical constants or random data.
